title: Book 1 — Clio, Chapter 125
paragraphs: Now there was a certain region of the Persian land overgrown with thorns, extending some eighteen or twenty furlongs in each direction. When all had come with what they had been commanded to bring, Cyrus ordered them to clear this region for cultivation within one day. When the Persians had achieved the task set before them, he ordered them to come to him on the next day bathed and clean. Meanwhile Cyrus, having gathered in one place all the flocks of goats and sheep and herds of cattle belonging to his father, slaughtered them and prepared with them to entertain the host of the Persians, and moreover with wine and other provisions of the most agreeable kind. So when the Persians came the next day, he made them recline in a meadow and feasted them. When they had finished dinner, Cyrus asked them whether what they had on the former day or what they had now seemed preferable to them. They said the difference was great, for the former day had for them nothing but evil, and the present day nothing but good. Taking up this saying, Cyrus proceeded to lay bare his whole design, saying: “Men of the Persians, thus it is with you. If you will do as I say, you shall have these and ten thousand other good things, with no servile labor; but if you will not, you shall have labors like that of yesterday, innumerable. Now therefore do as I say and make yourselves free: for I seem to myself to have been born by providential fortune to take these matters in hand, and I think you are not worse men than the Medes, either in other matters or in those which have to do with war. Consider, then, that this is so, and revolt from Astyages at once.”
